newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Deported Bangladeshis return from Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: Deported Bangladeshis return from Saudi Arabia.

text.p: More than 900 Bangladeshis deported from Saudi Arabia for travelling with forged documents or staying there illegally returned home on Tuesday, immigration officials said.
They arrived at Chittagong on board a Saudi-chartered ship. With Tuesday's batch, 7,712 out of 20,000 Bangladeshis ordered to leave Saudi Arabia have come home.
Officials said nearly 150,000 Bangladeshis worked in Saudi Arabia, but many had forged papers as a result of being cheated by employment agents.
Badiul Alam of Cox's Bazar, who returned on Tuesday, said he travelled to Riyadh in 1993 with a valid visa but stayed on after it had expired.
"I realised that I will become jobless back home. So I took the chance but was captured by Saudi authorities," he told reporters.
Another deportee, Mohammad Ali, said many expatriate workers, including Bangladeshis, "are facing arrest and deportation even if they have valid work permits".
Many returnees carried only hand luggage. Immigration officials gave them taka 200 ($5) to pay for transport to their homes.
